decisions.reason: The encrypted second channel sits on the firm's core cryptography and authentication knowledge, which lets it read customer feedback and keep improving the product through its own R&D, and it fits the binding mobile communication strategy.

Mobile PDF signing is close to the established offer and supports online contract signing, but as a narrow feature it may be absorbed into broader signing solutions after several years without separate visibility.
The multi-layer end-to-end architecture is the backbone of the integrated offering and draws most directly on the firm's deep security expertise, so dropping it would undermine the whole portfolio.

The email-to-app delivery robot uses the firm's secure messaging competence, but its niche use case and weaker market signals make rework or withdrawal fairly likely, though it remains a plausible part of the binding-communication direction.

The QR-based hardware token draws on the firm's hardware and authentication experience and serves regulated customers who need non-smartphone options, but app-based authentication keeps displacing hardware tokens, which raises the withdrawal risk.
